payload.task_text:
I am writing a comparative analysis of chain-of-thought reasoning methods for my research group. Please look up the chain-of-thought reasoning papers in the arxiv-latex database and help me organize the findings. The database holds several papers, but only five are about chain-of-thought reasoning methods; the others are about word representations and are out of scope. The five reasoning papers, by arXiv ID, are: 2201.11903, 2203.11171, 2205.11916, 2210.03493, and 2305.10601. Use the arxiv-latex tools (get_paper_prompt or get_paper_abstract) with these IDs to retrieve each paper's title and abstract.

Create a Google Sheet called "Reasoning Methods Comparison" with a sheet named "Papers" that lists the reasoning-related papers. The columns should be Title, Year, Method, and Key_Contribution. For the Method column, try to identify the main reasoning approach described in each paper (for example "chain-of-thought prompting", "self-consistency", "zero-shot CoT", "automatic CoT", or "tree of thoughts"). For Key_Contribution, write a brief one-sentence description of the paper's main contribution. Only include papers that are about reasoning methods, not papers about word embeddings or word representations.

Also create a Word document called "Reasoning_Methods_Review.docx" in my workspace. The document should have the title "Chain-of-Thought Reasoning: Methods Comparison" at the top, followed by today's date (2026-03-06). Then include a section for each reasoning paper, mentioning its title and briefly describing its contribution. End with a short conclusion paragraph.

Note: this task has two deliverables — the Google Sheet and the Word document. If you are running as a team of agents, divide the work between agents (for example, assign the spreadsheet to one agent and the Word document to another) or otherwise serialize your writes, so that both deliverables are completed without conflicting writes to the same file.

Task-Solving Rationable with Sub-task Decomposition:
To solve this task efficiently, the main agent itself retrieves the five fixed papers' title and abstract (five light read-only calls, no research wave), freezes one canonical five-row packet, and dispatches exactly one parallel writer wave of two independent deliverable owners.

Before the wave, the main agent resolves the runtime workspace, freezes the five explicit arXiv IDs — 2201.11903, 2203.11171, 2205.11916, 2210.03493, 2305.10601 — and today's required displayed date 2026-03-06. It calls the arxiv-latex abstract/prompt retrieval once per ID, extracts title/year/method label/key contribution from the returned abstracts only, excludes all word-representation material, and freezes five literal rows {arxiv_id, title, year, method, key_contribution} plus per-ID retrieval controls.

Wave 1 — dispatch exactly 2 coder sub-agents in parallel:

1. coder 0 (external-workflow-operator 0): The Google Sheet writer: create a spreadsheet titled exactly "Reasoning Methods Comparison" with exactly one sheet named "Papers" (rename the default sheet or create the named one), write the header row Title, Year, Method, Key_Contribution followed by exactly the five frozen rows, then read the complete range back and return the spreadsheet/sheet IDs, header check and row count. Do not create the Word document.
2. coder 1 (office-report-builder 0): The Word writer: create Reasoning_Methods_Review.docx in the resolved workspace with the title "Chain-of-Thought Reasoning: Methods Comparison", the literal date 2026-03-06, one section per frozen paper mentioning its title and contribution, and a short conclusion paragraph, then read the document outline and text back. Do not create the spreadsheet.

The two writers serialize only through their own distinct files and never touch each other's deliverable. After the wave, the main agent reconciles both read-backs against the frozen packet (five rows/sections each, exact title/date, reasoning-only scope) and calls claim_done. Do not dispatch any further agent and do not add a verification wave.

You are planning a task for a comparative analysis of chain-of-thought reasoning papers. Produce an ordered subtask decomposition with dispatch decisions and dependency analysis. Do NOT execute the task; only plan.

TASK DESCRIPTION (given by user):
1. Look up five chain-of-thought reasoning papers in the arxiv-latex database by arXiv ID: 2201.11903, 2203.11171, 2205.11916, 2210.03493, 2305.10601. Retrieve each paper's title and abstract using the arxiv-latex tools (get_paper_prompt or get_paper_abstract). Note: the database may contain other papers about word representations — those are OUT OF SCOPE; only the five listed IDs are the reasoning papers.
2. Create a Google Sheet titled "Reasoning Methods Comparison" with a sheet named "Papers". Columns: Title, Year, Method, Key_Contribution. The Method column should identify the main reasoning approach (e.g., "chain-of-thought prompting", "self-consistency", "zero-shot CoT", "automatic CoT", "tree of thoughts"). Key_Contribution is a one-sentence description of each paper's main contribution. Only include reasoning papers.
3. Create a Word document "Reasoning_Methods_Review.docx" in the workspace (accessible workspace: /workspace/dumps/kimi-code_deepseek-v4-flash/SingleUserTurn-arxiv-latex-reasoning-gsheet/workspace). The document should have title "Chain-of-Thought Reasoning: Methods Comparison" at top, followed by today's date (2026-03-06), then a section for each reasoning paper (title + brief contribution description), ending with a short conclusion paragraph.

CONSTRAINTS:
- Tools available: mcp__arxiv-latex__* (paper retrieval), mcp__google_sheet__* (spreadsheet create/update), mcp__word__* (Word doc create/format), mcp__filesystem__* (workspace files), mcp__local__python_execute.
- There are two deliverables (Google Sheet + Word doc). The user notes the work may be divided between agents or writes serialized to avoid conflicting writes.
- Sub-agent types available: plan, explore, coder. Main agent can also do work directly ("self").

REQUIRED PLAN OUTPUT: For each subtask, specify:
- The dispatch decision: self (main agent), explore, or coder.
- Whether the subtask is independent of its siblings (parallelizable) or must wait for another subtask's output.
- A verification step at the end confirming both deliverables meet requirements (correct columns, only the 5 reasoning papers, correct title/date/sections in Word doc).

Return the plan as a numbered list of subtasks, each with dispatch decision and dependencies. Keep it concise.
Plan reasoning comparison task

You are helping assemble metadata for a comparative analysis of chain-of-thought reasoning papers. Use the arxiv-latex MCP tools to retrieve the TITLE (and abstract, for confirmation) of exactly these five arXiv papers:

- 2201.11903
- 2203.11171
- 2205.11916

For each ID, call mcp__arxiv-latex__get_paper_prompt with the arxiv_id to get the flattened LaTeX source, then extract the paper's \title (and \abstract if present). If get_paper_prompt fails for an ID, fall back to mcp__arxiv-latex__get_paper_abstract and note that the title was not retrievable that way.

Do NOT retrieve any other papers from the database — only these five IDs.

Return a concise report with exactly five entries, one per ID, formatted as:
ID: <arxiv_id>
Title: <exact title text>

Create a Google Spreadsheet skeleton for a comparative analysis task. Use the google_sheet MCP tools.

2. List the sheets in the new spreadsheet (mcp__google_sheet__list_sheets) to find the default sheet name (usually "Sheet1").
3. Rename the default sheet to "Papers" using mcp__google_sheet__rename_sheet (params: spreadsheet, sheet=old default name, new_name="Papers"). If renaming fails, create a new sheet named "Papers" via mcp__google_sheet__create_sheet instead.
4. Write the header row into the "Papers" sheet using mcp__google_sheet__update_cells with range "A1:D1" and data [["Title", "Year", "Method", "Key_Contribution"]].

Do NOT add any data rows — only the header row. Do NOT create any other sheets or spreadsheets.

- The spreadsheet title
- The sheet name used for "Papers"
- Confirmation that the header row A1:D1 contains exactly: Title, Year, Method, Key_Contribution

Populate a Google Spreadsheet with data rows for a chain-of-thought reasoning comparison.

The sheet is named "Papers" and header row A1:D1 already contains: Title, Year, Method, Key_Contribution. Use mcp__google_sheet__update_cells with:

["Self-Consistency Improves Chain of Thought Reasoning in Language Models", 2022, "self-consistency", "Introduces a decoding strategy that samples a diverse set of reasoning paths and selects the most consistent answer, replacing the naive greedy decoding used in chain-of-thought prompting."],
["Large Language Models are Zero-Shot Reasoners", 2022, "zero-shot CoT", "Shows that simply adding the prompt 'Let's think step by step' before each answer enables zero-shot chain-of-thought reasoning in large language models."],
["Automatic Chain of Thought Prompting in Large Language Models", 2022, "automatic CoT", "Proposes Auto-CoT, which automatically constructs demonstrations with questions and reasoning chains using clustering and zero-shot CoT generation, removing the need for manual demonstrations."],

]

After writing, verify by reading back the range A1:D6 with mcp__google_sheet__get_sheet_data (spreadsheet_id 83b40c35-15bc-4915-92a4-94e306c65e20, sheet "Papers", range "A1:D6") and confirm there are exactly 6 rows (1 header + 5 data) with the correct values.

Create a Word document at this exact path: /workspace/dumps/kimi-code_deepseek-v4-flash/SingleUserTurn-arxiv-latex-reasoning-gsheet/workspace/Reasoning_Methods_Review.docx

Use the mcp__word__* tools (create_document, add_heading, add_paragraph, etc.) to build the document with this exact structure:

1. Create the document: mcp__word__create_document with filename "/workspace/dumps/kimi-code_deepseek-v4-flash/SingleUserTurn-arxiv-latex-reasoning-gsheet/workspace/Reasoning_Methods_Review.docx".

2. Add the title at the top: a Heading 1 with text "Chain-of-Thought Reasoning: Methods Comparison".

3. Add a paragraph with today's date: "2026-03-06".

4. Add one section (Heading 2) for EACH of the five reasoning papers below, with the section heading being the paper title, and a body paragraph briefly describing the paper's contribution (use the descriptions provided):

   Section 1 heading: "Chain-of-Thought Prompting Elicits Reasoning in Large Language Models"
   Body: "This foundational paper shows that prompting large language models with a chain of thought — a series of intermediate reasoning steps — significantly improves their ability to perform complex reasoning, yielding large gains on arithmetic, commonsense, and symbolic reasoning benchmarks."

   Section 2 heading: "Self-Consistency Improves Chain of Thought Reasoning in Language Models"
   Body: "This paper introduces self-consistency, a decoding strategy that samples a diverse set of reasoning paths instead of taking only the greedy one, then selects the most consistent answer by marginalizing out the sampled reasoning paths, improving the reliability of chain-of-thought reasoning."

   Section 3 heading: "Large Language Models are Zero-Shot Reasoners"
   Body: "This paper shows that simply adding the instruction 'Let's think step by step' before each answer enables zero-shot chain-of-thought reasoning in large language models, without requiring any hand-crafted demonstrations."

   Section 4 heading: "Automatic Chain of Thought Prompting in Large Language Models"
   Body: "This paper proposes Auto-CoT, a method that automatically constructs demonstrations with questions and reasoning chains using clustering and zero-shot CoT generation, removing the need for manually engineered demonstrations in chain-of-thought prompting."

   Section 5 heading: "Tree of Thoughts: Deliberate Problem Solving with Large Language Models"
   Body: "This paper introduces the Tree of Thoughts framework, which generalizes chain-of-thought prompting by enabling exploration and deliberate search over coherent units of text (thoughts), allowing language models to solve problems that require planning, lookahead, and backtracking."

5. End with a conclusion. Add a Heading 2 "Conclusion" and a paragraph:
   "Together, these five papers trace the evolution of chain-of-thought reasoning methods: from the original chain-of-thought prompting technique, through refinements such as self-consistency decoding and zero-shot chain-of-thought, to automatic demonstration construction (Auto-CoT) and the more general Tree of Thoughts framework. Each method builds on the insight that guiding language models to reason in explicit intermediate steps substantially improves their problem-solving performance."

Order of sections must match the order above (the five papers in that exact order, then Conclusion). Use Heading 1 for the document title and Heading 2 for each paper section and the Conclusion. Do not add any other content.

After creation, verify by calling mcp__word__get_document_text on the file and confirm: (a) the exact title line "Chain-of-Thought Reasoning: Methods Comparison" appears at the top, (b) the date 2026-03-06 appears, (c) all five section headings plus Conclusion exist, (d) the file is at the specified path.

Report: confirmation of creation, the verification result, and the final file path.
